findings.finding: We found BD=Fₙ, CD=Fₙ₊₁ ⇒ BC=Fₙ₊₂, AB–AC=Fₙ₋₁. The cyclic condition KNK′B forces a unique non‑degenerate triangle with AB+AC>BC; solving gives ratio CT·NB/(BT·NE)=BC/(AB–AC)=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. Hence a₂ₙ=F₂ₙ₊₂/F₂ₙ₋₁→φ³=2+√5. p=2,q=5 ⇒2²⁵ mod 99991=57447.

Incircle: BD=s−b=Fₙ, CD=s−c=Fₙ₊₁, a=BC=Fₙ₊₂. Using coordinates O(0,0), BC:y=−r, B(−Fₙ,−r), C(Fₙ₊₁,−r). Tangent points:  
F=(−2r²Fₙ/(Fₙ²+r²), r(Fₙ²−r²)/(Fₙ²+r²)),  
E=(2r²Fₙ₊₁/(Fₙ₊₁²+r²), r(Fₙ₊₁²−r²)/(Fₙ₊₁²+r²)).  
A from line equations → A=(r(sinE−sinF)/Δ, r(cosF−cosE)/Δ).  
K = second intersection of circumcircles (ABC) & (AEF). K′=reflection of K across EF. N=proj_D onto EF.  
Cyclic B,K,N,K′ ⇔ diff=0 gives unique r. Solving yields ratio R=(CT·NB)/(BT·NE) = (BD+CD)/(CD−BD)=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁.  
Thus aₙ=Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁. For even n=2m, a_{2m}=F_{2m+2}/F_{2m−1}→φ³=2+√5. So α=2+√5 ⇒ p=2,q=5. Compute ⌊2^{5²}⌋=2^{25}=33 554 432. 33 554 432 mod 99 991 = **57447**.
Key: aₙ = Fₙ₊₂/Fₙ₋₁ (ratio CT·NB/(BT·NE)). Derive from geometry: cyclic KNK'B forces AB–AC = Fₙ₋₁, giving ratio = BC/(AB–AC). So a₂ₙ → φ³ = 2+√5. p=2,q=5 → 2²⁵ mod 99991 = 57447.
